cur:catacombs-arles-apostles-strigil.summary: Two fields of strigils separate three standing figures: Christ in the centre and, at the ends, Saints Peter and Paul. The austere design focuses attention on Christ and the two princes of the apostles who founded the Roman Church.
facts: The museum states that it represents Christ at the centre with Saints Peter and Paul at the ends, and dates it to the end of the 4th century.

cur:objects-bnf-crucifixion-triptych-con.summary: In the arched central panel Christ hangs on a tall cross, with angels and the sun and moon above and the Virgin and St John standing on either side; below, the emperor Constantine and his mother Helena flank the foot of the cross, recalling the finding of the True Cross. The wings carry columns of saints in medallions joined by a vine-like band. The triptych unites the saving death of Christ with the imperial veneration of the cross that was so central to Byzantine piety.
facts: The pairing of the Crucifixion with Constantine and Helena links Christ's sacrifice to the legend of Helena's discovery of the True Cross in Jerusalem (iconographic tradition).

The object is digitised on Gallica by the Bibliothèque nationale de France, which describes it as an elephant-ivory triptych with the Crucifixion and saints, made in Constantinople in the second half of the 10th century.

cur:objects-tuotilo-tablets-evangelium-l.summary: The ivory tablet on the front cover of this gospel lectionary shows Christ seated in majesty within a mandorla, raising his hand in blessing, surrounded by the symbols of the evangelists and by angels, framed above and below by dense panels of vine-scroll. The cover is set in a frame of gems. It is the masterwork associated with the St Gall monk Tuotilo and one of the treasures of the abbey library.
facts: Tuotilo (died 915) was a monk of St Gall praised by Ekkehard IV a century later as poet, musician, painter and sculptor; Wikipedia notes that works in media other than music are attributed to him with less certainty.
The manuscript, called the 'Evangelium longum' for its tall format, is fully digitised on e-codices.
cur:objects-tuotilo-tablets-evangelium-l.notes: The date (c. 894) follows the Commons/e-codices metadata for the manuscript; the attribution of the carving to Tuotilo is traditional.

Q116244746.summary: Around the bowl of this silver incense burner, a medallion shows the bust of a youthful Christ with short curly hair and a halo, between figures of archangels. When incense rose from the censer during worship, the image placed the liturgy in the presence of Christ among his heavenly attendants.
facts: The Met notes that Christ is shown young to emphasise his divine vitality rather than his suffering, while the cross in his halo signals his identity.
A Greek inscription reads 'Of Saint John of the village of Attaroutha', naming the church to which it belonged.
It belongs to the Attarouthi Treasure, a group of liturgical silver from a village in Syria, acquired by the Met in 1986.
Q116244746.notes: Only one side is visible in the thumbnail; the archangels are partly seen.
